KOT-A4.title: Digital encoding: NRZ, NRZI and Manchester
KOT-A4.description:
Turn a sequence of bits into a line signal. Signal levels are written as + (high) and - (low).

  • NRZ (NRZ-L): 1 → +, 0 → -.
  • NRZI: the starting level is -; on a 1 the level flips, on a 0 it stays.
  • MANCHESTER (the IEEE 802.3 convention): each bit has two half-periods; 0 → +- (high to low), 1 → -+ (low to high).
KOT-A4.instructions: Input: the scheme name and the bit string (separated by a space). Output: the signal string.

KOT-A7.title: IPv4 subnet calculator
KOT-A7.description:
For an address in CIDR form (for example, 192.168.10.77/26) calculate the network address, the mask, the broadcast address, the first and last host and the number of hosts.

Network = IP AND mask; broadcast = network OR (NOT mask); number of hosts = 2^(32 − prefix) − 2.
KOT-A7.instructions: Input: IP/prefix. Output (6 lines): Network, Mask, Broadcast, First host, Last host, Number of hosts — in the format of the sample. The line labels are checked literally and stay in Uzbek as in the sample (Tarmoq, Maska, Broadcast, Birinchi xost, Oxirgi xost, Xostlar soni).

KOT-A8.title: Routing table: longest-prefix match
KOT-A8.description: When forwarding a packet, a router chooses among the routes matching the address the one with the longest prefix (the most specific). 0.0.0.0/0 is the default route. If no route matches, the packet is dropped.
KOT-A8.instructions: Input: n; n lines of network/prefix next_hop; q; q addresses. Output: for each address, the name of the next hop or DROP.

KOT-A9.title: Parsing an HTTP request
KOT-A9.description: Write the part of a server that parses a raw HTTP request received through a socket. The first line is the request line: the method, the path (with query parameters) and the version. Then come the headers up to an empty line (Name: value; header names are case-insensitive).
KOT-A9.instructions: Input: the text of the HTTP request. Output (6 lines): Method, Path, Query (the parameters or -), Version, Host (or -), Headers (their number). The line labels are checked literally and stay in Uzbek as in the sample (Metod, Yo'l, So'rov, Versiya, Host, Sarlavhalar).

KOT-A14.title: Checking firewall rules
KOT-A14.description:
A firewall checks a packet against the rule list from top to bottom and applies the first matching rule. If none matches — the default policy: deny.

A rule: ACTION protocol port source_network; the protocol is tcp, udp or any; the port is a number or * (any); the source is in CIDR form.
KOT-A14.instructions: Input: n; n rules; m; m packets (protocol port source_ip). Output: for each packet ALLOW k or DENY k (k is the rule number, from 1) or DENY default.
